title: How To Sell Personalized Products on Etsy and Shopify at the Same Time: A Seller's Guide
summary: Can you sell on Etsy and Shopify at the same time? Yes. Here's how to add Shopify to your Etsy shop and keep personalization running on both.
body_markdown:
Your Etsy shop has 400 reviews, a steady stream of orders, and a bestseller that people keep asking for in different names, colors, and birth months. It works. So why does a small voice keep suggesting you open a[Shopify](https://shopify.pxf.io/customily) store too?


Usually it's one of three things: you want your own customer list, you want control over your brand, or you're tired of competing on the same search results page as 50 near-identical listings. None of those reasons require you to leave Etsy. Most established sellers who add Shopify keep both, and that's what this guide is about: selling on Etsy and Shopify at the same time without doubling your workload.


## Etsy or Shopify or both?


The "Etsy or Shopify" question assumes you have to pick. You don't. The two platforms do different jobs.


**Etsy is a marketplace.** Buyers come to Etsy already looking for handmade, personalized, and[custom gifts](https://www.customily.com/) . You get built-in traffic and a trust signal, but you rent your audience. Etsy owns the search results, the customer relationship, and the rules.


**Shopify is your own store.** You bring the traffic (ads, email, social, SEO), but you own the brand, the customer data, the checkout, and the design. Nobody shows your buyer a competitor's listing next to yours.

The pattern we see often: Etsy brings in new buyers, Shopify turns the best of them into repeat customers. Etsy is the front door, Shopify is the living room.


## When it makes sense to sell on Etsy and Shopify at the same time


Adding[Shopify](https://shopify.pxf.io/customily) is worth the effort when:


- **Your Etsy sales are steady.** If you don't have proven products yet, fix that first. A second store won't fix a weak product.
- **You have a product people search for outside Etsy.** Personalized pet portraits, name necklaces, and[custom ornaments](https://www.customily.com/sell-personalized-products/ornaments) get searched on Google and Pinterest, not only on Etsy.
- **You want to run your own promotions.** Email flows, bundles, discount codes, and landing pages are far easier on Shopify.
- **You're worried about relying on one platform.** One policy change or one suspended listing shouldn't be able to stop your income.


Stay Etsy-only for now if you're still testing products, if you have no time to market a second store, or if your whole advantage is Etsy's built-in search. A Shopify store with no traffic is just an expensive empty shop.


### How to sync Etsy and Shopify (and what "sync" really means)


Search for "Etsy and Shopify sync" and you'll find tools promising a one-click link between the two. Before you pick one, decide what you actually need synced. There are four separate things:


1. **Listings.** Getting your Etsy products into Shopify so you don't rebuild them by hand.
2. **Inventory.** Keeping stock counts matched so you don't oversell.
3. **Orders.** Seeing orders from both channels in one place.
4. **Customer and personalization data.** Keeping the details each buyer entered (names, dates, text, uploads) attached to the right order.


Here's how sellers usually handle the first one, which is the "copy Etsy listings to Shopify" step:


- **A marketplace connector app.** Several Shopify apps can import Etsy listings and keep inventory in sync. A few that list Etsy support on the Shopify App Store: Shopify's own Marketplace Connect (aimed mainly at listing your Shopify catalog on marketplaces and managing those orders), DPL, ShopList, QuickSync, shopUpz, and Etsy Sync & Importer by velopLab. Their listings describe syncing some mix of products, inventory, prices, and orders, and the plans differ in order and product limits, so read each one's current description before installing.
- **CSV export and import.** Export your Etsy listings, reformat the file to Shopify's product import template, and upload it. It's slower, but it gives you full control and you see exactly what's going over.
- **Manual rebuild for your top products.** For your 10 best sellers, rebuilding the listing from scratch is often worth it. Etsy titles are stuffed with keywords for Etsy search. A Shopify product page needs to read like a real product page, with a clean title, better photos, and a description written for Google and for humans.


Whichever route you pick, don't expect listings to arrive clean. Check titles, variants, images, and shipping settings on every imported product. And remember: variants and personalization options often don't carry over properly, which brings us to the part that trips up most personalized-product sellers.


## The real problem: personalization across two channels


If you sell standard products, running two channels is mostly a listings and inventory problem. If you sell[personalized products](https://www.customily.com/our-features) , there's a bigger issue. Every order needs details from the buyer, and those details have to become a print-ready file or a production instruction.


On Etsy, buyers typically type their personalization into a text box. On Shopify, you can do much more: **show a live preview** , offer fonts and colors, let buyers upload photos. But if you handle these two channels differently, you end up with two workflows, two sets of files, and twice the chance of a mistake.


This is where a personalization tool earns its place. With[Customily](https://www.customily.com/) , you can run personalization on both channels from one setup:


**On Shopify** , buyers get a live preview. They type a name, pick a font, choose a design, and see the result on the product before they pay. That cuts "wrong name" and "that's not what I expected" messages.


**On Etsy** , Customily works in two ways:


- **Etsy's personalization mode.** Customily captures the personalization data from the order and generates the print file. There's no live preview in this flow, so it fits sellers who are happy with Etsy's standard buying experience.
- **Live preview after purchase.** The buyer tries options before buying, then receives a personalization link after the order to confirm the final details.


In both cases, the order data feeds an automatically generated print-ready file, so you aren't copying names out of messages and into a design tool by hand.


Once orders from both channels are flowing in, you manage them in one place: view order details, edit print files if you need to, and get real-time updates. From there you can send orders directly to a POD partner or export a CSV if you work with your own production partner. Files can be PDF, PNG, JPG, AI, EPS, DXF and other formats, and you can download all files in bulk. If you print at home, laser engrave, cut, or embroider, the same logic applies.

If you sell on Shopify and Etsy, each platform has its own subscription, and transaction fees don't bundle across platforms. Your designs, assets, and settings are shared across your Customily account, so you build once and manage everything from one place. The fee counts unique personalized items, not quantity, so five identical personalized mugs in one order count once.


The point isn't that Customily is magic. The point is that **the personalization setup should be built once and used on both channels** , not rebuilt every time you add a sales channel.


## Managing orders, fulfillment, and support across both channels


Once both stores are live, the daily work is where most multichannel sellers struggle. A few habits make it manageable.


**Pick one place to see all orders.** Switching between two dashboards to find what needs printing is how orders get missed. Whatever tool you choose, orders from both channels should end up in one queue.


**Keep production the same.** The same product should be produced the same way whether it was sold on Etsy or Shopify. Same file specs, same supplier, same quality check. Customers on both channels should get the same product.


**Decide how you'll handle inventory.** If you make to order, stock counts matter less. If you hold blanks, decide who gets priority when stock is low, and consider a buffer so you don't oversell on the busier channel.


**Write your support answers once.** Questions like "Can I change the name?" or "When will it ship?" come up on both platforms. Keep one set of answers and adapt the wording to each channel's messaging tool.


**Price on purpose.** Etsy and Shopify have different fee structures, so you can't copy prices blindly. Here's a quick example on a $40 personalized item with shipping included in the price (US, no ads, before cost of goods):


- **Etsy:** $0.20 listing fee + $2.60 transaction fee (6.5%) + $1.45 payment processing (3% + $0.25) = about $4.25, or roughly 10.6% of the sale.
- **Shopify (Basic plan, Shopify Payments):** $1.46 card processing (2.9% + $0.30), about 3.7% of the sale, plus your monthly plan cost.


Etsy costs more per sale, and you're paying for that built-in traffic. Shopify costs less per sale, but you pay for your own traffic and the monthly plan. Some sellers price the same on both. Others price slightly differently or run Shopify-only bundles and offers. Either can work, but decide deliberately and run your own numbers. Etsy's optional Offsite Ads fee and Shopify's plan tier will change the math.


## How to launch Shopify alongside your Etsy shop: a short plan


1. **Pick 5 to 10 products to start.** Your proven bestsellers, not your whole catalog.
2. **Set up your Shopify store.** Choose a clean theme, add your policies, and connect payments and shipping.
3. **Bring over your listings.** Use a connector app or CSV, then clean up titles, photos, and descriptions by hand.
4. **Set up personalization on your Shopify product pages.** Add your live preview and personalization options, and test them on mobile.
5. **Connect your order flow.** Make sure Shopify orders and Etsy orders both land where your production process starts.
6. **Place test orders on both channels.** Check that the print file comes out right from each one.
7. **Send your first traffic.** Add your store link to your packaging, your email list, your social profiles, and your Etsy shop announcement where allowed.
8. **Review after 30 days.** Look at traffic sources, conversion, and margin per channel. Double down on what's working.


## Mistakes to avoid when selling on Etsy and Shopify


- **Copying your Etsy listing word for word.** Etsy-style keyword titles read badly on a brand store and can hurt your Google performance.
- **Ignoring Etsy's rules.** Read Etsy's current policies before you point buyers to your own store. Don't use Etsy messages or packaging to steer buyers in ways the rules don't allow.
- **Launching without traffic.** Plan how people will find your Shopify store before you build it.
- **Letting prices drift.** If the same item is a lot cheaper in one place, you'll confuse customers and cannibalize your own store.
- **Treating personalization as an afterthought.** It's the part most likely to break, so test it first and test it often.
- **Doing everything at once.** Start small. You can add more products after the workflow is smooth.


## Add Shopify without giving up Etsy


You don't have to choose. Keep Etsy for discovery, build Shopify for ownership, and set up personalization once so both channels run on the same workflow.

### Frequently Asked Questions


**Can I sell on Etsy and Shopify at the same time?**


Yes. Many sellers run both. Etsy brings marketplace discovery, and Shopify gives you a store you own. Check each platform's terms and keep your listings accurate on both.


**Do Etsy and Shopify sync automatically?**


Not out of the box. They're separate platforms. Third-party apps can connect them and sync some things, such as listings and inventory, but what's included varies by app, so check what each one actually syncs.


**Can I copy my Etsy listings to Shopify?**


Yes. You can use an import app, or export your Etsy listings to a CSV file and upload them to Shopify. Expect to clean up titles, images, and variants afterward, especially for personalized products.


**Is it better to use Etsy or Shopify for personalized products?**


It depends on where you are. Etsy is strong for being discovered by gift shoppers. Shopify is stronger for branding, repeat customers, and richer personalization on the product page, like a live preview. Many sellers use both.


**Do I need two separate personalization setups?**


No. You can run personalization for both channels from one tool, so that orders from Etsy and Shopify produce print-ready files the same way. That saves time and cuts down on mistakes.


**Will adding a Shopify store hurt my Etsy shop?**


Having a second channel doesn't change your Etsy ranking by itself. What matters is following Etsy's policies and keeping your Etsy shop active and well run.
